description: Group B Strep can pass from mother to baby during delivery and, if not detected and treated early, can lead to an infection that causes a brain injury.
shortAnswer: Group B Streptococcus is a type of bacteria that can be passed from mother to baby during delivery and if not detected and treated early enough can lead to an infection that causes a brain injury. Group B Strep can easily be prevented: if the bacteria is detected neonatal antibiotics can be prescribed to eliminate it.

faq.q: What complications can a Group B Strep infection cause in a newborn?
faq.a: The brain injury can lead to a host of medical issues, including cerebral palsy, spastic quadriplegia, seizure disorders, an inability to swallow, communications deficits, incontinence and permanent pain. Other complications of Group B Strep infections are sepsis, pneumonia, meningitis, and death.

faq.q: What if my doctor did not test for Group B Strep before delivery?
faq.a: If the diagnostic test is not ordered, there are well settled protocols for observing the infant after delivery to detect Group B Strep infection. The doctors and nurses taking care of your baby are responsible to follow these protocols so they can detect the infection and administer antibiotics immediately.

faq.q: Can a delay in antibiotics for Group B Strep cause brain damage?
faq.a: Delay in starting antibiotics can result in catastrophic injuries to a newborn, including severe and permanent brain injuries.
